minutes.headline: Water commissioners heard PFAS treatment options for the idle Hickory Hills well; funding article goes to annual meeting.
minutes.summary: Most of the meeting was spent on PFAS treatment for the inactive Hickory Hills well, with a Weston and Sampson engineer and a Stantec representative presenting options and a draft scope. Commissioners also covered the Mass Ave water main, a T-Mobile tower lease RFP, annual meeting article assignments, and a developer's water main plan. Minutes and the water main plan were moved; outcomes were not audible.

votes.motion: Approve the water main plans as submitted, with hydrant locations per the superintendent and fire department approval.

budget_items.topic: State revolving loan fund for PFAS
budget_items.what_was_said: Presenter said state revolving fund money is growing this year, PFAS is eligible for zero interest loans, and loan forgiveness is possible.
Large filter systems cost far more than the small containerized setup; full plants run to millions while quick pilot systems are much cheaper.
Media replacement every two years was estimated at a modest cost including trucking and disposal.
Stantec gave a rough range for the scope and piloting; the state does not fund pilots and design up front, though retroactive reimbursement is being considered.

budget_items.topic: Annual meeting article for PFAS pilot funding
budget_items.what_was_said: An article at Saturday's annual meeting seeks funding for the long-term pilot study; the amount was unclear in captions.

budget_items.topic: Water main pipe prices and availability
budget_items.what_was_said: Pipe costs have risen sharply and zinc-coated pipe is unavailable; the Mass Ave main project is about a million dollars and was not put on the SRF list.
New RFP proposal offers annual rent with an escalator over five-year terms, compared with the current monthly payment.

decisions.decision: Commissioners favored a temporary, inexpensive pilot treatment setup on gravel rather than a permanent building, pending further review.
Review the Stantec scope after Saturday's annual meeting vote and discuss at the next meeting.
Another engineering firm will be invited to present at next week's meeting.

what_happened.line: Water commissioners spent most of the meeting on PFAS treatment options for the idle Hickory Hills well, hearing from two engineering firms.
Commissioners favored a temporary, low-cost pilot treatment setup on gravel over a permanent building, pending further review.
The Stantec scope for the pilot study will be reviewed after Saturday's annual meeting vote and discussed at the next meeting.
A motion to approve a developer's water main plans, with hydrant locations set by the superintendent and fire department, was made; the outcome was not audible.
Another engineering firm will be invited to present at next week's meeting.

why_it_matters: The PFAS pilot is the first step toward treating a well the district is not currently using, and the cost of treatment would eventually reach water customers' rates unless state loans or reimbursement cover it.
Residents at the annual meeting will be asked to vote on an article funding the long-term pilot study.
